summary: Multi-tenant session cookie prefix misalignment prevents Support Console login for some orgs
description:
Issue summary:
Users from a subset of orgs (multi-tenant customers and internal support test orgs) are intermittently unable to log into the Support Console. The identity provider (Okta) completes auth, but the Support Console reports a 401/403 on session exchange. This started after the identity-proxy v2.3.1 rollout on 2026-03-12.

Impact:
- Internal agents cannot access the Support Console for affected orgs (blocks incident handling).
- Automated runbooks that rely on the support-tool session API return 401s for affected org tenants.

Suspected root cause (initial hypothesis):
identity-proxy v2.3.1 introduced a default cookie prefix change from "redwood_sess_org_" to "rwd_sess_" when org-scoped cookies are enabled. Some legacy support-tool SDKs and our console client still look for the old cookie name and do not send the newly-prefixed cookie, causing the session lookup to fail at the session-store layer.

Why unique / notes:
This is not a pure Okta claim mapping bug; the Okta assertion is fine and tokens are issued. The failure surface is at browser->console where the cookie name mismatch prevents the session exchange header/cookie from being presented to the console backend.
steps_to_reproduce: Using an affected org account, navigate to https://support-console.redwood.internal and click Sign in with SSO.
Okta authentication completes and redirects back to the console callback (/auth/callback?code=...).

Observe that the browser receives Set-Cookie: rwd_sess_<orgid>=<token>; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.internal but the console client looks for cookie named redwood_sess_org_<orgid> and does not attach session to API requests.
API request to /api/v1/support/tickets returns 401 with body: { "error": "session not found" } while Okta logs show successful assertion for the user.
Reproduced reliably on affected org test accounts; unaffected orgs show the old cookie or have the client patched to look for both prefixes.
observed_behavior: Support Console callback receives new cookie name (rwd_sess_<orgid>) but downstream API calls fail with 401/session-not-found because client code only attaches redwood_sess_org_<orgid>.
expected_behavior: Session cookie name used by identity-proxy and session-store should match the console/support-tool client expectations, or clients should accept both prefixes during a migration period.
logs:
curl -v 'https://support-console.redwood.internal/auth/callback?code=...' -H 'Cookie: ' -i
* Received HTTP/2 200
< Set-Cookie: rwd_sess_12345=eyJhbGci...; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.internal; Secure; HttpOnly
*
HTTP/2 200
{"message":"redirected to console"}

identity-proxy access logs (2026-03-12T22:14:02Z):
INFO request_id=req-7b2c GET /auth/callback 302 set-cookie=rwd_sess_12345
Okta auth log: successful assertion for user u=alice@acme.co, org_id=12345, auth_time=2026-03-12T22:13:59Z
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 deploy of identity-proxy v2.3.1 changed default cookie_prefix config when org_scoped_cookies=true (ops change recorded in deploys channel).
A canary of v2.3.1 in eu-west rolled back after unrelated perf alerts; us-east remained. Affected orgs correlate with orgs that had legacy console-client versions (<=1.14.2).
Session-store shows sessions exist under both cookie-name spaces for some orgs (migration in progress), but clients only lookup the old name. Example keys: redwood_sess_org_12345 vs rwd_sess_12345.
Temporary workaround verified by manually setting document.cookie to include redwood_sess_org_12345 with the current token value — console session resumes normally for the user.

Identity team suggests two remediation paths: (A) roll back cookie-prefix change in identity-proxy to preserve old cookie name; (B) make console client tolerant to both prefixes and perform a coordinated rollout.
mitigation_workaround: Short-term: ops can set a response header in identity-proxy to set an additional legacy cookie name (Set-Cookie: redwood_sess_org_<orgid>=<same token>) for affected orgs. Manual JS workaround: support agents can run a snippet to copy the rwd cookie into the legacy cookie name. Both are stopgaps until clients/servers are aligned.
resolution: Triage in progress. Engineering is preparing a PR to make the console client accept both cookie prefixes and to add a compatibility shim in identity-proxy. No production rollback yet; planned approach is staggered: client patch (canary), identity-proxy compatibility header, then cleanup. Target: client canary 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-17.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 Priya Patel: Ticket created after oncall report #support. Several internal agents reported regressions when handling tickets for customer org 12345.

2026-03-13 10:05 Diego Morales (identity-proxy): Confirmed v2.3.1 change. Default cookie_prefix variable was modified during refactor. Investigating quick toggle to restore legacy prefix for affected orgs.
2026-03-13 11:20 Sasha Ivanov (console): Console client 1.14.2 only checks for redwood_sess_org_<orgid>. We have a branch that probes both names; can run canary in staging today.
2026-03-13 13:45 Liam Chen: I'll own coordinating patch and canary. Assigning to myself. Preparing PR to add fallback lookup and add server-side Set-Cookie compatibility header.
2026-03-14 08:30 Ops (note): Temporary header shim applied to identity-proxy for org 12345. Affected users in that org report restored access. Need wider rollout guidance.
2026-03-14 09:00 Legal/Security: confirm that dual-cookie approach is acceptable from a security perspective (HttpOnly, Secure preserved).
